relevance_note: One patient carries a heterozygous TNFAIP3 variant: 'a previously unreported truncating variant in TNFAIP3 (c.2199C>A, p.Cys733*)', classified by the authors as a VUS, alongside a RAD21 variant.
method_note: Read the full Markdown by hand; no table transcription (the only table is the abbreviations list). The JSON was assembled by a short Python script from values I chose while reading, then every span was checked verbatim against the paper by script. One proband; no relatives described with clinical or genetic data (the 'maternal history of cleft palate' is ambiguous about who is affected, so no row for the mother). The authors do not diagnose HA20 in this patient: the diagnoses are CdLS (CdLS4, RAD21) and generalized pustular psoriasis, and the TNFAIP3 variant is called a VUS. No HA20 hallmark (oral/genital ulcers, fever, inflammatory markers) is mentioned, so those checklist items are 'not reported'. The RAD21 variant is recorded because the paper attributes it unambiguously to the proband. No wet-lab functional assay was done; only in silico AlphaFold structural modelling and UniProt Variant Viewer lookups, so functional_evidence_statement is 'not reported'. 'Neurocognitive features include dysprosody and limited social interaction' was taken as central nervous system involvement (observed); these are neurodevelopmental, not inflammatory, features. Short stature plus low weight-for-age was taken as growth failure (observed). Contradictions and inconsistencies in the paper: (1) the Figure 2 and Figure 3 legends call both the RAD21 and TNFAIP3 variants 'de novo', but no parental testing is described anywhere, so inheritance is 'not reported' (rule 8); (2) Methods say alignment and UCSC use were GRCh37/hg19, but the figure legends give GRCh38/hg38 positions; the RAD21 location is also given as 'chr8:10,673,499–10,658,686' in section 2.3.1, which does not match 'chromosome 8: position 116,852,561 (GRCh38/hg38)' in the Figure 2 legend (the legend value was recorded); (3) the RAD21 transcript is printed as NM_006265.2 and also as 'Transcript: NM_006265.1' (NM_006265.2 recorded); (4) the RAD21 classification varies: 'pathogenic for CdLS type 4' (abstract), 'likely pathogenic' (2.1), 'probably pathogenic' (2.2.1), 'pathogenic ... according to ClinVar' (discussion); 'likely pathogenic' recorded; (5) for both variants the text says the change is 'on the Glycine amino acid', which conflicts with p.(Gln436*) and p.(Cys733*); (6) the TNFAIP3 transcript is printed as NM_001270507.1 and also as 'Transcript: ENST00000612899.5' (NM recorded); the text also prints 'c.2199 C>A' with a space once; (7) the phrase 'upper-limb reduction defects that range from subtle phalangeal abnormalities to oligodactyly (missing digits)' in the proband description (2.1) is identical to the general CdLS description in the Introduction, and neither it nor hypertrichosis appears in the Methods physical examination (4.1), so whether the proband has oligodactyly is uncertain; recorded as stated in 2.1; (8) an earlier local skin biopsy was 'compatible with pemphigus foliaceus', and the later biopsy 'confirmed the diagnosis of pustular psoriasis'; the earlier reading was not recorded as a feature; (9) the RAD21 UniProt ID is given as O60216 in Methods and Q99215 in the Discussion (not used). Hospitalization is mentioned but no treatment, so treatment_summary is 'not reported'. Age at onset is not given as an age (only an '8-month history' at age 13), so onset is 'not reported' and the 8-month history is in severity_or_detail.
